findings.title: Journal search with an apostrophe crashes the API (SQL built by string interpolation, injectable)
findings.steps: On /journal type it's into Search (or open /journal?q=it's directly). Or curl GET /api/journal?q=it%27s
findings.expected: Search treats the text literally and returns matching entries (or 'No entries match')
findings.actual: API returns 500 Internal Server Error; page shows 'Could not load the journal.' Search term is f-string-interpolated into the LIKE clause (backend/routers/journal.py list_entries), so q=zzz%' OR 1=1 OR '%'=' returns every entry (SQL injection). % and _ also act as wildcards.
findings.evidence: curl q=it's -> 500; q=' OR 1=1 -- -> 500; injected OR 1=1 returned all 3 entries. In browser, typing it's showed 'Could not load the journal.'

findings.title: Retrying an Add entry after a lost/timed-out response creates a duplicate entry
findings.where: Plant detail page, Journal 'Add entry' / POST /api/journal
findings.steps: On /plants/1, type an entry; make the POST reach the server but the response fail (network timeout). Page shows 'The garden server could not be reached.'; click Add entry again.
findings.actual: Two identical entries are created; count jumps from 2 to 4 entries' worth (two DUPTEST rows). No idempotency key or dedupe.
findings.evidence: After retry the list showed 'DUPTEST 1794483387265' twice on 12 Nov 2026

findings.title: Journal load errors offer no retry
findings.where: /journal page and plant detail Journal section
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (e.g. 503) and open /journal, or navigate from /plants to a plant
findings.expected: Error message with a Retry button that refetches without reloading
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' text is shown, with no retry control; on plant detail the only way to recover is a full reload
findings.evidence: Retry/Try again button count = 0 on both pages under a 503 response

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout: a hanging search spins forever and keeps showing stale results
findings.steps: On /journal, make GET /api/journal hang, type 'Lettuce' in Search, wait 12+ seconds
findings.expected: Request fails after 10 s with an error and retry
findings.actual: 'Loading entries…' stays indefinitely while the previous search's results (for 'Thinned') remain displayed under the new query. No timeout is configured in useApiFetch/useApiClient, so Add/Save buttons would also stay on 'Saving…' forever if the server hangs.
findings.evidence: After 12 s: 'Loading entries…' with the old 'Lettuce / Thinned the seedlings.' card still shown

findings.title: Out-of-range ids crash journal endpoints with 500
findings.steps: curl POST /api/journal with plant_id 99999999999999999999, or PUT /api/journal/99999999999999999999
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow); no upper bound on ids
findings.evidence: All three requests returned 'Internal Server Error 500'

findings.title: Journal accepts absurd past dates such as year 0001
findings.expected: Reject implausible dates with a visible reason (only future dates are rejected)
findings.actual: 201 Created; entry dated 1 Jan 1 is stored and sorts to the bottom

findings.title: Client 'today' and server date.today() can disagree, refusing today's entry
findings.steps: Use the app in a time zone ahead of the server (e.g. UTC+10 in the morning) and add an entry for today
findings.expected: Entry for the user's today is accepted
findings.actual: Client allows the date (todayIso uses local time) but the server compares against its own date.today() and returns 'Journal date cannot be in the future.'
findings.evidence: Code: frontend utils/format.ts todayIso vs backend schemas.py not_in_future
